newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian fund says Sidanko owns Purneftegaz stake.
newsitem.headline: Russian fund says Sidanko owns Purneftegaz stake.

text.p: The Russian Federal Property Fund said on Tuesday that the assets of oil group Sidanko included a 38 percent stake, equivalent to 50.7 percent of the voting shares, in AO Rosneft-Purneftegaz.
The assets of OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sidanko) were listed in the official announcement of a tender for 51 percent of Sidanko.
However the stake in Purneftegaz is subject to a legal dispute.
It is not clear whether the disputed status of Purneftegaz could affect the validity of the tender for Sidanko, for which bids are being accepted until January 9.
The Purneftegaz stake was originally allocated to the state oil holding company Rosneft but in November a Moscow court recognised a claim by Sidanko to own the stake.
Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Tumarkin told Reuters that Rosneft intended to appeal against this decision.

The fund set a starting price of $129 million for the 51 percent stake, which appears to be the same as the 51 percent state stake currently managed by MFK bank under the government's shares for loans programme.
MFK bank is associated with Uneximbank, which won an investment tender for 34 percent of Sidanko in September.

Winners of the tender must also pay Sidanko $161 million within one year, and transfer 73.70 million shares in refinery AO Angarskaya Neftekhimicheskaya Kompaniya to Sidanko within a month. Sidanko already owns 38 percent of the Angara refinery.
Sidanko is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating units are Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz.
